gold_with_text_not_included.reason: I1 and I2 not met: despite volume terminology in the title and interpretation, the Methods specify GM-density testing and the Results report a left ACC density difference. A whole-brain voxel-wise GM-volume contrast is not demonstrated. The original cross-sectional MRI study compares 9 PTSD survivors with 16 trauma-exposed survivors without PTSD (I3 met). It performed whole-brain VBM rather than only ROI analyses (E1 not met), and reported significant between-group density findings, so it is not a null-only or within-group-only study (E5 and E6 not met).

I2 not_met: the whole-brain voxelwise contrasts test GM density, not GM volume; the authors attribute the ACC effects to shape and location differences. Actual volume comparisons are restricted to ACC regions and are nonsignificant, consistent with Table 1. I1 is met through empirical MRI regional volumetry, and I3 through matched normal controls. E1 and E6 are not met because the paper also reports significant whole-brain density findings, although these do not satisfy I2.

I1 and I2 not met: although the abstract and discussion describe volume reductions, the structural Methods analyze smoothed tissue intensities/density, and the morphological Results and Figure 2 report GM-density differences. No separate GM-volume analysis or qualifying whole-brain GM-volume contrast is demonstrated. This empirical English-language MRI study compares 12 DSM-IV PTSD fire survivors with 12 trauma-exposed survivors without PTSD (I3 met). It reports significant whole-brain density and functional between-group differences, so E1, E5 and E6 are not met; E2-E4 also do not apply.

I2 not met and E1 met: both FreeSurfer volume comparisons and VBM analyses were restricted to selected prefrontal, parietal and posterior midline ROIs; the Methods explicitly state that statistical VBM analyses were masked for these ROIs. Whole-brain MRI acquisition and comparisons of total cortex/total GM do not establish a whole-brain voxel-wise contrast. I1 and I3 are met. Table 3 reports regional PTSD-control differences, so E6 is not met despite the failure of VBM findings to survive conventional correction for multiple comparisons. E2-E5 do not apply.

I2 not met: a separate whole-brain PTSD-versus-eligible-control GM volume contrast is not demonstrated. Table 1 and Figure 1 pool 24 PTSD patients with 29 major-depression patients against 29 trauma-exposed healthy controls. Tables 2–5 report symptom correlations. The null PTSD-versus-depression comparison does not use an eligible control population. Original structural MRI and eligible trauma-exposed controls establish I1 and I3. Separate PTSD-versus-healthy-control significance is unreported, rather than established as null (E6 unclear).
